subtype: Approach: pre-mortem before the plan starts [Thinking]
passage: On the veranda of her family's farmhouse, Shalini wrote a line at the top of a fresh page: exam day, and under it, "I failed because..." Then she made herself keep going. Phone, she wrote, since the videos on Uncle's handset never stop. A sick week, because monsoon fevers go through the village every year. Skipped sleep, from the night-before panic. Chandrika, the neighbour, leaned over the wall with a guava. "What is this, a funeral notice?" "A plan," said Shalini. Beside each reason she added a step: phone in the cupboard until six, three chapters photocopied at the shop in town in case of fever, lights out by ten. Chandrika read it and reached for a pen. "Now it can't surprise me," Shalini said.

qa.q: What reasons for failure did Shalini list?
qa.a: Phone, a sick week and skipped sleep.

qa.q: What does Shalini's line 'Now it can't surprise me' suggest about how Shalini feels?
qa.a: Shalini feels calmer and more in control, because each fear now has a protective step beside it. 🙂

qa.q: What alternative approach could Shalini add beyond the list, and why?
qa.a: A weekly mock paper marked against the answers would show which chapters slip, while the list only guards against risks Shalini has already predicted.

qa.q: How might Chandrika see the page of failure reasons?
qa.a: Chandrika first finds it gloomy and jokes about a funeral notice, but after reading the steps sees a practical plan and reaches for a pen to make one too.

grounding: The student imagines exam day with revision failed, lists likely causes such as phone, illness and skipped sleep, and adds a protective step for each before the plan begins.

subtype: Approach: pre-mortem before the plan starts [Thinking]
passage: Four weeks before his final exams in Toronto, Ivan sat at the kitchen table with a blank sheet and tried something his sister Mina had learned at university. "Imagine it's exam morning," she said, "and revision went badly. Why?" Ivan closed his eyes. "I was on my phone every night till one." He wrote it down. "I got sick in week two and lost five days." Down. "I stayed up cramming and was a zombie." Down. Then Mina said, "Now fix each one before it happens." Phone: charges in the hallway after ten. Sick week: every Sunday afternoon left free for catch-up. Sleep: lights out at eleven, written on the fridge. Ivan looked at the sheet. It felt odd to plan for failure, but now the plan had shields.

qa.q: Where does Ivan's phone charge after ten?
How might Ivan have felt imagining that revision had failed?
qa.a: He probably felt uneasy at first, picturing the failure, then steadier once each reason had a fix.

qa.q: What other risk could Ivan add to his list?
qa.a: A hard subject he keeps putting off, with a step such as doing it first each day, so the plan protects against that too.

qa.q: How might Mina see her brother's sheet?
qa.a: Mina may feel pleased that the university trick helped, and see the plan as stronger for having its shields built in.

grounding: Shows a student imagining revision has failed, listing likely reasons and adding a protective step for each before starting.

subtype: Approach: pre-mortem before the plan starts [Thinking]
passage: In the last class before study leave, Zeenat Ma'am wrote on the board: "It is 15 March. Your exams went badly. Write down why." The room went quiet. Sachin stared at his page, then started. "Phone. I kept watching matches." "Got flu, lost a week." "Slept four hours before Maths." Around him others were scribbling too. "Now," said Zeenat Ma'am, "next to each reason, write one thing you will do from tomorrow so it can't happen." Sachin thought. Phone: hand it to Mummy from seven to ten. Flu: keep Sunday free as a buffer. Sleep: no studying after eleven, however scared. He underlined the last one twice. On his way out, Zeenat Ma'am glanced at his page and nodded.

qa.q: What date did Zeenat Ma'am write on the board?
Why did Sachin underline the sleep step twice?
qa.a: He seems to know that fear pushes him to stay up late, and was worried enough about it to make that step extra firm.

qa.q: What would make Sachin's plan stronger?
qa.a: Telling his family about the steps, like the phone arrangement with Mummy, so he isn't relying only on himself when stress rises.

qa.q: How does Zeenat Ma'am seem to see Sachin's page?
qa.a: Her nod suggests she approves of the concrete steps he has attached to each risk.

grounding: Shows a class pre-mortem where a student lists why revision might fail and plans a protective step for each reason.
